effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per rule of the Mantle specification's TRANSFER section (payload, proof, gas, validation, execution, example), in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-ledger that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot); the Mantle Ledger section (note spendability, output validation, consuming and creating notes) is audited by another brief, so trace here what TRANSFER itself requires and point to that section where a rule is the ledger's.

The section defines the TRANSFER operation: payload (inputs, outputs), proof (the zero-knowledge signature over the inputs), execution gas, validation and execution, with a worked example.

Where the section lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/ops/transfer.rs and ops/op.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the TRANSFER payload. ops/proof_zk_and_ed.rs: the proof type a transfer carries.
- ledger/src/mantle/mod.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): validation and execution of a transfer against the ledger (balance, fee, note consumption and creation). ledger/src/update.rs: the ledger update that applies it. ledger/src/intent.rs: the transfer intent type.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; core/src/mantle/fixtures/ shows how transactions and ledgers are built in tests. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
